DejaVu.notes: DejaVu family. Use DejaVu Sans directly if bundled as a webfont; otherwise Noto Sans or Arial is a practical sans fallback.

FreeMono.notes: FreeMono is a GNU FreeFont monospace face. Cousine is metrically close to Courier-style screen use; Roboto Mono is a common web fallback.

FreeSans.notes: FreeSans is a GNU FreeFont sans face in the Helvetica/Arial style. Arimo is a practical webfont fallback.

FreeSerif.notes: FreeSerif is a GNU FreeFont serif face in the Times style. Tinos is a practical webfont fallback.

Orbitron_Light.notes: Named Orbitron Light. Use the Orbitron webfont with a light weight.

Roboto_Thin.notes: Named Roboto Thin. Use the Roboto webfont with weight 100.

Satisfy.notes: Named Satisfy. Use the matching Satisfy webfont.

Yellowtail.notes: Named Yellowtail. Use the matching Yellowtail webfont.

efontCN.notes: efont Simplified Chinese bitmap family. Noto Sans SC approximates script coverage, but not the bitmap texture.

efontJA.notes: efont Japanese bitmap family. Noto Sans JP or M PLUS 1p approximates script coverage, but not the bitmap texture.

efontKR.notes: efont Korean bitmap family. Noto Sans KR approximates script coverage, but not the bitmap texture.

efontTW.notes: efont Traditional Chinese bitmap family. Noto Sans TC approximates script coverage, but not the bitmap texture.

lgfxJapanGothic.notes: LovyanGFX Japanese Gothic family. M PLUS 1p is a close practical webfont candidate; Noto Sans JP is a robust fallback.

lgfxJapanGothicP.notes: Proportional variant of LovyanGFX Japanese Gothic. Use the same webfont stack as lgfxJapanGothic.

lgfxJapanMincho.notes: LovyanGFX Japanese Mincho family. Noto Serif JP is the safest webfont fallback.

lgfxJapanMinchoP.notes: Proportional variant of LovyanGFX Japanese Mincho. Use the same webfont stack as lgfxJapanMincho.

Font0.notes: Small 6x8 GLCD-style bitmap sans. Use a pixel font fallback; exact origin is not identified from the family name.

Font2.notes: Larger proportional bitmap sans. Similar visual role to a small embedded LCD UI font.

Font4.notes: Large proportional bitmap sans. Pixel-style web fonts approximate the texture, but not the exact glyph design.

Font6.notes: LovyanGFX source says Font 6 is intended to display numbers and time. It contains space, digits, colon, minus, period, a/p/m, and pipe as narrow space. The image is rounded LCD-style, so custom canvas rendering is closer than a generic text font.

Font7.notes: LovyanGFX source identifies this as a 7-segment font intended for numbers and time. DSEG7 Classic is the closest practical webfont fallback.

Font8.notes: LovyanGFX source describes this as an Arial 75 pixel height font intended to display large numbers.

Font8x8C64.notes: LovyanGFX source cites https://github.com/hugovangalen/C64_Font8x8 as the original source. Prefer a C64-style bitmap webfont fallback when available.

AsciiFont8x16.notes: Fixed 8x16 ASCII bitmap. VGA/DOS terminal-style fonts are closer than modern monospace fonts.

AsciiFont24x48.notes: Fixed 24x48 ASCII bitmap. Treat as a scaled terminal bitmap face.

TomThumb.notes: Known TomThumb GFX font. If licensing and packaging are acceptable, using TomThumb itself as a webfont gives the closest preview.
